title: Spectral-Inspired Neural Operator Learning with Limited Data and Unknown Physics

problem.claim: Learning PDE dynamics from limited data when the governing physics is unknown is challenging.

gap.claim: Existing neural PDE solvers generally require large datasets or known physics, limiting applicability.

contributions.claim: SINO models complex systems from five trajectories without explicit PDE terms.
SINO learns Fourier multipliers as functions of frequency indices to represent differential operators and capture high-order derivatives and global/local couplings.
SINO models nonlinear effects through multiplicative interactions on derivative features followed by spectral low-pass filtering for de-aliasing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on 2D and 3D PDE benchmarks reportedly show state-of-the-art performance and accuracy improvements of 1–2 orders of magnitude.
With five training trajectories, SINO reportedly outperforms data-driven methods trained on 200 trajectories.
SINO reportedly remains predictive on challenging out-of-distribution cases where other methods fail.

narrative_sequence.summary: Limited-data learning of PDE dynamics with unknown physics is challenging.
Existing neural PDE solvers depend on large datasets or known physics.
SINO addresses the challenge using five trajectories without explicit PDE terms.
The method learns frequency-dependent Fourier multipliers and uses multiplicative derivative interactions with spectral low-pass filtering.
Benchmark experiments report strong accuracy and performance under limited-data and out-of-distribution settings.

source_observation.claim: A spectral representation with learned frequency-dependent multipliers is reported to capture differential operators without explicit PDE terms.

interpretation.claim: Learning operator structure in the frequency domain may reduce dependence on handcrafted physics representations.

application.claim: This approach may be considered for operator-learning problems with limited data and unknown governing equations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish performance beyond the reported PDE benchmarks or identify the data and computational requirements in detail.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not provide details about the five trajectories, out-of-distribution settings, or computational cost.
